scope: MEAS: independent review of the public score.json and two-page sheet pack (Edward Neeman). Covers source, licence and attribution; the line-269 token correction against the French first edition; a converter re-run with --config; bar order; gates; the sheet pack; pitch bands at the constrained bars and the final chord; a register-aware per-bar lag scan; and segment-wise chroma DTW against the d'Albert recording. Not aural review.

observations.finding: This is display only, as for Op. 25/6. The .krn's three *8va spans open after barlines 21, 31 and 41 and close (*X8va) after barlines 23, 34 and 49. In the rasterised pack those passages are engraved at sounding pitch with many ledger lines.

The candidate equals the public file; results equal checks; the config and audio hashes match.

barMap.finding: All 1,141 notes lie inside their bar, and bar times increase. check_contract.py prints 'ok … 51 bars; 1141 notes; 2 source-defined voices'. Both pages were rasterised and inspected: 9 justified systems, bars 1–51, and a final barline. The pack is identical to the d'Albert pack once DOM ids are stripped, and index.json is byte-identical.

order.finding: Bars 1–51 once. The print has no repeat signs (see printComparison).

Verovio: 1,142/1,142 notes, 0 timing differences. The regenerated MusicXML is byte-identical to the Neeman and d'Albert derivatives. independentChecks.tokenCorrection: EXT: Schlesinger first edition (CFEO 25-1-Sm, BnF VM8 S 140, plate M.S. 2427), p. 32, bar 21 under 8va, viewed at full IIIF resolution. The fourth sixteenth is an octave one staff step below the preceding F-flat octave, which carries flats. The fourth sixteenth itself has no accidental, so under the G-flat key signature it is E-flat. This supports correcting line 269's malformed `16edee-'>JJ`/`16dee-` to E-flat7/E-flat6 (`16eeee-`/`16eee-`).
independentChecks.printComparison: EXT: the same print, pp. 32–33. 2/4, 51 bars in systems of 4/5/5/5/5 and 5/5/5/6/6, no repeat signs, ritenuto in bar 36, p at the bar-37 reprise, and the final barline after bar 51. Bar 1 has the C-natural octave on its fourth sixteenth, and bar 37 opens on held G-flat4/G-flat5. This agrees with the encoding. The encoded source itself is the Lemoine issue (025-1b-LE-009), which was not viewed.
independentChecks.registerLagScan:
Correlating pitch-resolved note onsets with per-band CQT flux, 46 of 51 bars fit best within 0.1 s. The exceptions are:
- bars 35 (+0.68 s, gain 1.17), 40 (−1.16, 1.06) and 47 (−0.56, 1.04), which have small gains. Bar 35's D-flat2/D-flat3 and E-flat5 entry, published at 44.42 s, rises at 44.42/44.39/44.41 s.
- bars 48–49 (−0.64/−1.16 s), where the B-flat5/G-flat6 notes repeat across both bars, so the scan cannot separate them. The bands confirm both bars. In bar 48 (published 61.681 s), B-flat5 and G-flat2 rise at 61.61 s, E-flat6/C-flat7 at 61.86/61.88 s (published 61.95), and the second-half E-flat6/C-flat7 and D-flat6/B-flat6 at 62.44–62.47 and 62.60–62.61 s (published 62.47/62.61). In bar 49 (published 62.74 s), B-flat5/G-flat6 rise at 62.78 s and G-flat2 at 62.68/62.78 s.
independentChecks.crossRecording: Segment-wise chroma DTW into d'Albert's first pass agrees within ±0.27 s for all of bars 1–36 (median 0.117 s). Bars 45–48 have identical right-hand pitch classes, so chroma DTW cannot place them, and d'Albert's second pass is checked in its own review.
independentChecks.constraints: The bar-37 constraint (q73 → 48.96 s) lands on the C-flat4 (MIDI 59) rise at 48.97 s (+28 dB). Bar 37's D-flat3/B-flat3/G-flat4/G-flat5 entry, published at 47.701 s, rises at 47.73–47.76 s. The bar-49/50 constraints match the band rises listed above.

overlays.finding: Bars 35–39 (ritenuto and reprise) and bars 45–51 land on the measured energy.
